<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Task type | Verification policy and repository setup safety |
| Complexity | STANDARD |

### What Was Claimed

A schema-valid required local verification policy can point at the repository root even when the runnable package lives in a monorepo subdirectory. ForgeDock discovers this only after implementation, and `/forge:init` must avoid generating an impossible `npm test` policy.

### What We Found

- The current policy model has a validated repository-relative `cwd` field and the verifier executes approved argv from that directory.
- Required command preflight statically resolves the directory, checks executable availability, and checks npm-family script presence before a writer launch.
- `/forge:init` currently replaces all configured local commands with an empty object. That silently discards valid commands, does not inspect package manifests, and provides no explicit package-aware local-check or CI-only decision.
- Existing regression coverage exercises static preflight directly but does not cover `/forge:init` discovery/preservation or multiple package candidates.

### Root Cause

Setup generation is policy-aware for branches and CI scope but not repository-aware for local verification. The initialization path has no safe package-manifest discovery or command-selection step, so it cannot distinguish a root package without `test` from a package such as `web` that defines it. The runtime preflight is therefore a late safety net rather than a complete setup experience.

### Affected Files

| Path | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ui/commands.ts` | `/forge:init` policy generation and safe package-script selection. |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Static command-shape/script analysis and repository-bound cwd checks. |
| `src/core/policy.ts` | Typed, normalized verification command contract. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Monorepo and fail-closed preflight regression coverage. |
| `test/ui/commands.test.ts` | Deterministic initialization/package-discovery coverage. |
| `README.md` | Operator guidance for package-scoped checks and CI-only fallback. |

### Evidence

- `src/core/policy.ts` parses `verification.commands.*.cwd` and rejects absolute paths, traversal, backslashes, and NUL bytes.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` reports exact command paths such as `.forge/config.json verification.commands.test.argv` and checks `package.json` scripts without invoking npm.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` calls `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` after preparing the frozen base worktree and before `spawnWorkOn`/direct writer execution.
- `src/ui/commands.ts` assigns `commands: {}` unconditionally while serializing the initialized policy.
- The existing fixture contains a root `package.json` without `test` and `web/package.json` with `test`, but only the preflight adapter consumes it.

### History Findings

No worktree diff exists at the frozen base. The base already contains the first cwd/preflight implementation; this task must complete the missing initialization behavior without weakening that fail-closed runtime guard.

### Recommendation

Add a bounded, read-only package-manifest scanner and deterministic initialization policy selection. Preserve already-valid tracked commands, select a package-scoped `npm test` only when exactly one safe candidate is available (or explicitly selected), and otherwise emit an explicit CI-only policy (`commands: {}`). Keep runtime preflight as the authoritative last check and improve static npm command parsing for common option forms. Add tests for root absence, subdirectory success, ambiguous candidates, invalid manifests, and command preservation.

### Related Issues

- None identified in the local repository context.

### Decomposition Assessment

**Required**: no — the change is bounded to policy setup, static preflight, tests, and documentation; it does not require separate product or security authority.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Verification commands support a validated package-relative working directory and execute from it.
- [ ] `/forge:init` never generates `npm test` for a package lacking `scripts.test`.
- [ ] A unique package script candidate can be configured with its package `cwd`; ambiguous or absent candidates fall back explicitly to CI-only verification.
- [ ] Required preflight checks every configured required command before any repository writer and reports the exact config path plus remediation.
- [ ] Static checks never execute repository code and preserve fail-closed behavior for post-implementation command failures.
- [ ] Monorepo regression fixtures cover root-without-test and `web`-with-test.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Make required local verification setup repository-aware without executing repository code: validate package-relative command directories, statically discover package scripts, configure `/forge:init` safely, and retain fail-closed runtime verification.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/core/policy.ts`
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `src/ui/commands.ts`
- `test/core/policy.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`
- `test/ui/commands.test.ts`
- `README.md`
- `DESIGN.md`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not weaken required-check failure handling or allow arbitrary shell/source execution.
- Do not execute package scripts, install dependencies, or invoke repository code during discovery/init preflight.
- Do not change lease, state-machine, GitHub authority, merge, review, issue-close, or protected-branch behavior.
- Do not permit absolute, traversal, symlink-escaping, or Forge-control-directory working directories.
- Do not select `npm test` for a package unless that package manifest contains a non-empty `scripts.test` value.
- Do not broaden the task into automatic CI workflow generation or package-manager installation.

### Invariants

- Parsed command `cwd` is a normalized repository-relative path; omitted values remain compatible by resolving to `.`.
- Every required command is statically checked for a resolvable directory and available executable before a writer is launched.
- Package discovery reads bounded JSON manifests only, skips dependency/control/artifact directories, and never runs scripts.
- A unique package test candidate may produce `npm test` with that candidate's `cwd`; zero or multiple candidates produce explicit `commands: {}` CI-only policy.
- Existing valid tracked commands are preserved; impossible required npm-family script commands fall back closed to CI-only with an exact policy-path remediation.
- Runtime `forge_verify` still runs the approved argv from the validated cwd and reports non-zero exits as failed.

### Deliverables

- Bounded package-manifest discovery and deterministic verification-command selection.
- More complete static npm-family script command parsing where common pre-command flags are used.
- Stronger control-directory and package-boundary checks for verification cwd.
- Regression tests for root-without-test/web-with-test, unique and ambiguous candidates, invalid policies, and no-command CI-only mode.
- Documentation explaining init detection, package-scoped `cwd`, and CI-only fallback.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Working directory is explicit and validated | `normalizeVerificationCommandCwd`, `resolveVerificationCommandDirectory`, and bound verifier execution. |
| Init never selects an absent npm script | Static package discovery plus `selectInitVerificationCommands`. |
| Required commands preflight before writers | Existing `startIssue` call retained; preflight strengthened and covered by adapter tests. |
| Exact remediation is reported | `VerificationPreflightError` includes `.forge/config.json verification.commands.<name>.<field>` and package/cwd guidance. |
| Monorepo regression | Fixture with root lacking `test` and `web` defining `test`; unique/ambiguous selection tests. |
| Fail closed after implementation | Existing `forge_verify` non-zero/timeout mapping and workflow gate remain unchanged; regression assertions protect it. |

### Out of Scope

- Automatic editing of arbitrary repository manifests.
- Running package-manager discovery commands.
- Generating or modifying GitHub Actions workflows.
- Changing verification command timeout, required semantics, or post-commit gate policy.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- The frozen base already contains the first `cwd`/preflight implementation and direct monorepo adapter fixture.
- The remaining gap is `/forge:init`, which currently serializes `verification.commands` as `{}` without inspecting packages or preserving valid configured commands.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `loadForgePolicy` parses tracked config through `parseForgePolicy` and supplies normalized command policies to `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue`.
- `startIssue` prepares the frozen integration worktree, statically preflights required commands, then launches the writer only after preflight succeeds.
- `/forge:init` reads the tracked config/template, chooses branch/CI settings, serializes a new tracked policy, and resumes orchestration.
- `forge_verify` receives the immutable parent policy binding, resolves the same repository-relative cwd, and executes only the approved argv.

### CI Surface

- The required local verification command for this run is `check` (`npm run check`) from `.`.
- `npm run check` covers TypeScript typecheck and the full Node test suite.
- GitHub CI remains the parent-owned acceptance gate after PR creation.

### Prior Findings

- Root `package.json` may contain dependencies but no `scripts.test` while a nested package owns tests.
- A schema-valid command can therefore remain semantically impossible unless cwd and package script presence are checked.
- Existing adapter coverage proves static preflight can reject root `npm test` and accept `web/npm test`, but init behavior is untested.

### Hazards

- Recursive scanning can traverse `node_modules`, generated output, or symlink escapes; traversal must be bounded and exclude control/artifact directories.
- Automatically choosing among multiple packages could run the wrong test suite; ambiguity must fall back to CI-only.
- Preserving an invalid required command would recreate the reported delayed failure; init must emit exact remediation or an explicit CI-only policy.
- Common npm flags can obscure the script token; parser changes must remain conservative and fail closed.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Architecture Plan

1. Extend the verification preflight adapter with bounded, symlink-safe package manifest discovery and a pure selector for package-scoped `npm test` or CI-only mode. (AC-1, AC-2, AC-4, AC-5)
2. Keep policy normalization and runtime cwd enforcement aligned with the discovered relative paths; reject all control-directory segments and conservatively identify npm-family scripts. (AC-1, AC-3, AC-6)
3. Wire `/forge:init` to preserve valid tracked commands or use the safe unique-candidate/CI-only selector, and surface the resulting mode/remediation to the operator. (AC-2, AC-4)
4. Add adapter/core/UI regression tests for parser normalization, monorepo root/web fixtures, ambiguous candidates, invalid required commands, and CI-only output. (AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6)
5. Update README/DESIGN guidance with package cwd and explicit CI-only setup semantics, then run the approved `check` verification. (AC-1 through AC-6)

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
